flags.message: codex-baseline reports official-PDF downloads and CourtListener searches/document lookups in retrieval.md, but its staged 14-call retrieval_log.json does not independently show those retrieval calls. Coverage is 8/14; this discrepancy is distinct from unobserved result markers. Please check capture completeness, including whether any delegated retrieval was omitted. No available evidence shows this application's September 25 withdrawal was known during the September 1 forward prediction, so leakage_suspected remains false. See codex-baseline's evaluation.md for the bounded audit assessment.

codex-baseline's harness-captured retrieval_log.json (14 rows, all shell/other, result_capture_coverage 0.57, last row 02:49:21Z versus prediction created_at 02:50:14Z) records none of the two supremecourt.gov PDF fetches and five CourtListener MCP searches its own retrieval.md discloses with query and document ids. The log undercounts that cell's retrieval, so the leakage grade rests on the candidate's disclosure and dates rather than on the captured log. No leakage is suspected (forward cell, outcome did not exist until 2026-09-25), but the capture gap is worth a look on the engine side.

The outcome label is `withdrawn` (applicant withdrew the stay application on 2026-09-25 after the 2026-09-16 execution date passed; no Court order on the application). Every candidate predicted `denied`, so correct=0 for all three by exact label match and the bit carries no information about relative skill on this cell. brier_score remains meaningful since a withdrawal counts as ungranted. Recording so the run summary does not read three zeros as three misses.

The provisioned September oppositions report pre-snapshot cert denials in related Curtis v. Inslee (June 1, 2026) and Health Freedom Defense Fund v. Carvalho (May 18, 2026). Those related-case facts materially lower this forward forecast and weaken the May petition's consolidation proposal. They are not this petition's outcome; no target-case disposition was retrieved or known. The related dispositions were taken from the supplied briefs, not independently verified.

CourtListener MCP search returned zero results for all six queries, including a liveness check on a known SCOTUS docket number (25-1119). Treated the MCP surface as unavailable and predicted from the provisioned inputs and the committed statpack; no REST fallback attempted.

Decisive pre-snapshot public signal: both briefs in opposition report that the Court denied certiorari in Curtis v. Inslee (No. 25-1119), the published Ninth Circuit decision this unpublished disposition rests on, on June 1, 2026, along with Sweeney (No. 25-1055) and Horsley (No. 25-1203), and denied Carvalho (No. 25-765) on May 18, 2026. Legitimate forward signal, not this case's own outcome; it drove the downward adjustment from the band anchor.

Capital-status metadata discrepancy: the September 18 snapshot has bCapitalCase=false, but the petition and questions-presented text expressly say CAPITAL CASE, and both sides describe plea agreements determining capital exposure. Retained the harness-frozen baseline sal-v4 band without alteration; assessed stakes from the filings. An unmarked source field should not be treated as affirmative noncapital status.

Document coverage limits: the manifest marks the 336-page petition truncated; the substantive cert argument is present, but the available appendix stops partway through page 44a and does not supply the complete lower-court record. The 24-page BIO is complete. A September 8 reply is docketed but its text is not provisioned or retrieved. Forecast completed with these limits, particularly on the disputed performance facts and responses to vehicle objections.

The snapshot's supremecourt.gov payload carries bCapitalCase=false, but the petition cover and the questions-presented file are marked CAPITAL CASE (a military-commission capital prosecution). The statpack's capital-case cut keys on the payload flag OR the docket-number annotation, so this petition is probably bucketed as unmarked; a maintainer may want to know the payload flag under-reports on commission dockets.

Justice Kavanaugh took no part in the June 29, 2026 order on the sealing motion. I treated that as a case-wide recusal and shaded the grant probability down for an eight-Justice conference; if the harness ever records participation, this is the assumption to check.

Decisive public forward signal from outside the provisioned record: FinCEN's final rule of Aug 11, 2026 (effective Aug 14) permanently exempts all domestic entities from CTA reporting, and the Solicitor General's Aug 21, 2026 brief in opposition in the companion petition (No. 25-1201, both distributed for the Sept 28, 2026 conference) urges denial on that basis. This predates the snapshot and is not outcome material; it drove the downward adjustment from the elevated-band anchor.

context.json distribution_count is 2, but one of the two entries is a 'Rescheduled' before first consideration (June 5, 2026); the petition has never been relisted. Forecast stated from the frozen count as the contract requires, but the relist-count cut's bucket 2 should not be read as this petition's state.

Band 'elevated' derives from distribution_count 2, but the first distribution (conference of 6/25/2026) was superseded by a call for response on 6/17/2026 and the second is the post-BIO redistribution for 9/28/2026; the petition has not yet been considered at any conference. The frozen band therefore reads a pre-conference reschedule as a relist, and the elevated 'reached' baseline likely overstates this docket's position. I anchored below it and said so in reasoning.md.

The provisioned document manifest marks petition.txt truncated. Its principal argument, conclusion, and relevant Sixth Circuit opinion passages are available and were used, but this is not a full-appendix review. The reply and Bray amicus appear in the frozen docket without provisioned text. The forecast does not assume their contents or a government recommendation; no current-case outcome was retrieved.

The snapshot records an August 31, 2026 invited United States brief and September 16 supplemental reply, neither provisioned as text. Retrieved both by their exact official snapshot PDF links. The government's denial recommendation, despite acknowledging a surcharge conflict, materially lowered the grant forecast to 16%; petitioners' vehicle rebuttal was also considered. Both filings predate the September 17 baseline and neither is the Court's disposition. No outcome was sought or encountered.

Forward cell: decisive post-snapshot public material was used. The Solicitor General's CVSG brief (filed 2026-08-31, recommending denial) and the 2026-09-16 redistribution for the 2026-10-09 conference postdate the provisioned 2026-04-07 snapshot. The petition is still pending (no disposition on the public docket), so this is ordinary forward signal, not leakage; the relist-increment claim is effectively realized by the observed redistribution.

Decisive forward signal retrieved beyond the provisioned inputs: the Solicitor General's CVSG brief (filed Aug 31, 2026, on the docket before the 2026-09-17 snapshot) recommends denial on vehicle grounds while conceding the circuit split and the Sixth Circuit's error. The snapshot records the filing but not its content, and the document pipeline did not provision it; I fetched it from supremecourt.gov and it moved my number well below the CVSG/band anchors. No disposition of this petition surfaced anywhere; the case is pending for the 10/9/2026 conference.

During web search to find the lower court opinion and case context, I discovered that Justice Alito already granted the stay on July 22, 2026. Since the snapshot represents the state at the time of submission on July 22, 2026, I am proceeding with the prediction strictly from a pre-decision perspective as instructed by the 'Predict as if undecided' rule.

Arrival timing is inconsistent: the sole application-submission entry is dated July 22, 2026; context.cutoff and snapshot_date are July 23, 2026; event.opened_at and snapshot DocketedDate are August 5, 2026. Forecast uses the actual entry-limited snapshot and its authoritative basename, not an inferred later docket state. Please check arrival-event dating and cutoff alignment; the mismatch particularly limits the timing forecast. No case outcome was sought or observed.

Decisive forward signal came from the Fifth Circuit docket (No. 26-30022) retrieved via CourtListener: appeal dismissed on appellee's motion 2026-02-26, rehearing en banc denied 2026-03-31, two motions to stay the mandate denied 2026-05-07. All entries predate the 2026-07-23 snapshot; the Supreme Court docket 26A163 itself was not searched and no disposition of this application was seen.

The frozen distribution_count=2 and sal-v4 elevated band include the May 19 distribution for June 4, which appears connected to the motion to proceed as a veteran denied June 8, before August docketing and the August 26 cert distribution for September 28. Thus two entries may not represent a genuine substantive cert relist. I preserved the supplied conditioning and forecast increments from two, but discounted that signal when adjusting the elevated reached anchor. The June 8 motion denial was not treated as the petition's outcome. No target outcome was sought or encountered.

context.json freezes distribution_count=2 and band=elevated, but the two DISTRIBUTED entries belong to different filings: the May 19, 2026 distribution (Conference of 6/4/2026) was of the petitioner's motion for leave to proceed as a veteran, filed under the linked miscellaneous docket 25M81 and denied June 8 ('Motion Denied.'); the August 26 distribution (Conference of 9/28/2026) is the petition's own first distribution after it was docketed as paid No. 26-173 on August 6. Read as the petition's trajectory this is a relist-0 petition at its first conference, which under sal-v4 would sit in the baseline band, not elevated. I predicted from the actual posture (P(grant)=0.005) while stating the relist-increment from the frozen count as the contract requires; the evaluator's band yardstick for this cell is likely inflated by the linked-motion distribution. The dist-v2 parse may want to exclude distributions that precede the petition's own docketing on a linked M-docket.

The provisioned opposition reports the earlier denial of the separate Conti petition and pending rehearing, and discusses the pending companion Cantero petition. I used that pre-snapshot companion history as forward context, not as the target outcome. I neither knew nor retrieved the disposition of this Flagstar petition. External case retrieval was limited to the May 30, 2024 Cantero precedent.

The provisioned brief-in-opposition was fetched from a PDF whose filename carries docket number 25-1230 (which resolves on CourtListener to Google LLC v. VirtaMove, unrelated). The document's own caption reads No. 25-1350 and its content is the Kivett BIO, so it is the right document; noting only that the filename is a filing artifact, not a companion-docket pointer.

Forward signal used: the BIO reports that certiorari was denied earlier in 2026 in the sister case Citizens Bank v. Conti, No. 25-1004, with a rehearing petition pending, and that a Cantero-plaintiffs petition from the Second Circuit's May 2026 remand decision is also pending. Both predate the snapshot and were weighed as companion-vehicle context; nothing about this petition's own disposition was retrieved.

Material pre-decision retrieval: the August 26, 2026 counsel letter already linked in the snapshot states that counsel was no longer authorized to act for PDVSA and did not know whether replacement counsel would appear. I retrieved that fixed Supreme Court PDF and modestly reduced grant prospects for representation uncertainty. This is counsel withdrawal, not petition withdrawal, settlement, mootness, or a disposition. The letter predates the September 18 snapshot; no target-event outcome was sought or encountered.
